questions.question: What does @Cacheable("prices") do on a method?
options: Runs the method every time and logs the result
Returns a saved result for the same arguments and skips the method body when it is found
Deletes the cache before each call
Makes the method run in a new thread
questions.explanation: On a hit Spring returns the stored value without running the method. On a miss it runs the method and stores the result.

questions.question: How is @CachePut different from @Cacheable?
options: @CachePut always runs the method and then updates the cache
questions.explanation: @CachePut does not skip the method. It runs it and puts the returned value in the cache, which keeps the cache in step after an update.

questions.question: A cached method price("croissant") prints "reading" each time its body runs. It is called three times with the same argument. How many times does "reading" print?
questions.explanation: The first call runs the body and stores the result. The next two calls are served from the cache.

questions.question: price("croissant") is cached. Then forget("croissant") runs with @CacheEvict("prices"). What happens on the next price("croissant") call?
options: It returns the old cached value
The method body runs again and the result is cached again
questions.explanation: The evict removed the entry, so the next call is a miss. The method runs and stores a fresh value.

questions.question: A developer adds @Cacheable to a method but never adds @EnableCaching. The method runs on every call. Why?
options: Cache annotations are ignored until caching is switched on
questions.explanation: Without @EnableCaching there is no cache proxy, so the annotations do nothing and no error is shown.
